items.stem: Which is the correct definition of the term "ligand"?
options: A central metal atom or ion surrounded by ligands bonded by dative covalent (coordinate) bonds.
An element whose highest-energy electron is in a d subshell.
Attraction into a magnetic field shown by species with unpaired electrons, such as many transition metal ions.
A molecule or ion with one or more lone pairs of electrons that forms a dative covalent bond to a central metal ion.
items.answer: A molecule or ion with one or more lone pairs of electrons that forms a dative covalent bond to a central metal ion.
items.markingKey: Ligand: a molecule or ion with one or more lone pairs of electrons that forms a dative covalent bond to a central metal ion.

items.stem: Why is scandium not classed as a transition element?
options: Its only ion, Sc³⁺, has no d electrons
items.answer: Its only ion, Sc³⁺, has no d electrons
items.markingKey: Sc³⁺ is 3d⁰.

items.stem: Why do transition elements show variable oxidation states?
options: They have very high first ionisation energies
The 3d and 4s electrons have similar energies, so different numbers can be lost or shared
items.answer: The 3d and 4s electrons have similar energies, so different numbers can be lost or shared
items.markingKey: Successive ionisation energies rise gradually.

items.stem: What is the oxidation state of copper in Cu₂O?
items.markingKey: Sum of oxidation states equals the overall charge: copper is +1.

items.stem: State the oxidation state of chromium in CrO₄²⁻ and give the electronic configuration of chromium in this oxidation state.
items.answer: +6; 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶

items.stem: Omar is writing a report on manganese, a first-row transition element. One of its compounds contains MnO₄²⁻. In industry, MnO₂ catalyses the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide. (a) Write the electronic configuration of a manganese atom. (b) Deduce the oxidation state of manganese in MnO₄²⁻ and give the electronic configuration of manganese in this state. (c) Predict, with a reason, whether compounds containing MnO₄²⁻ would be paramagnetic.
items.answer: (a) 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d⁵ 4s² (b) +6; 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d¹ (c) Yes: manganese in the +6 state has 1 unpaired electron(s).
items.markingKey: (a) 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d⁵ 4s² [1] (b) oxidation state [1]; configuration [1] [2] (c) Yes: manganese in the +6 state has 1 unpaired electron(s) [1]

items.stem: Which property of transition elements explains their catalytic activity?
options: They can change oxidation state and adsorb reactants using d orbitals
items.answer: They can change oxidation state and adsorb reactants using d orbitals
items.markingKey: Electron transfer and surface bonding.

items.stem: Explain why transition elements and their compounds often act as catalysts.
items.answer: They can change oxidation state readily, accepting and donating electrons in intermediate steps; and they can adsorb reactants onto their surfaces using d orbitals, weakening bonds.
items.markingKey: variable oxidation states [1]; adsorption / d orbitals [1] [2]

items.stem: What is the oxidation state of iron in [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻?
items.markingKey: Sum of oxidation states equals the overall charge: iron is +3.

items.stem: What is the electronic configuration of the Co³⁺ ion?
items.answer: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d⁶
items.markingKey: Cobalt atom 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d⁷ 4s²; lose 4s electrons first: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d⁶.

items.stem: Describe and explain the characteristic properties of the transition elements Ti to Cu, referring to electronic configurations, variable oxidation states and catalytic activity.
items.answer: Definition (incomplete d subshell in an ion); configurations including Cr 3d⁵4s¹ and Cu 3d¹⁰4s¹; 4s lost before 3d; variable oxidation states because 3d/4s similar in energy, max state rises to Mn (+7) then falls; examples MnO₄⁻, Cr₂O₇²⁻, VO₂⁺; catalysis: variable oxidation states (Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺) and adsorption (Fe, V₂O₅); complexes and colour; Sc and Zn not transition elements.
items.markingKey: definition [1]; configurations with exceptions [2]; variable oxidation states explained [2]; catalysis with examples [2] [7]

items.stem: Which is the correct definition of the term "coordination number"?
options: A ligand that forms several dative bonds to one metal ion, e.g. hexadentate EDTA⁴⁻.
A ligand that forms two dative bonds to a metal ion, e.g. ethane-1,2-diamine or ethanedioate.
A ligand that forms one dative bond to a metal ion, e.g. H₂O, NH₃, Cl⁻, CN⁻.
The number of dative (coordinate) bonds from ligands to the central metal ion.
items.answer: The number of dative (coordinate) bonds from ligands to the central metal ion.
items.markingKey: Coordination number: the number of dative (coordinate) bonds from ligands to the central metal ion.

items.stem: Why does [CuCl₄]²⁻ have a lower coordination number than [Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺?
options: Chloride ions are larger than water molecules, so fewer fit around the metal ion
Cu is in a different oxidation state
items.answer: Chloride ions are larger than water molecules, so fewer fit around the metal ion
items.markingKey: Ligand size.

items.stem: Which complex shows optical isomerism?
items.answer: [Ni(en)₃]²⁺
items.markingKey: Three bidentate ligands: non-superimposable mirror images.

items.stem: What is the oxidation state of nickel in [Ni(H₂O)₆]²⁺?
items.markingKey: Overall charge minus ligand charges gives +2.

items.stem: For the complex [Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂], state the oxidation state of platinum, the coordination number, the shape and a bond angle.
items.answer: +2; coordination number 4; square planar; 90°

items.stem: For the complex [Fe(EDTA)]⁻, state the oxidation state of iron, the coordination number, the shape and a bond angle. Identify the type of ligand present and state, with a reason, whether the complex shows stereoisomerism.
items.answer: +3; coordination number 6; octahedral; 90°; ligand: EDTA⁴⁻ (hexadentate); optical isomerism
items.markingKey: +3 [1]; 6 [1]; octahedral [1]; 90° [1]; ligand type [1]; stereoisomerism decision with reason [1] [6]

items.stem: Samuel adds concentrated hydrochloric acid dropwise to aqueous copper(II) sulfate, which contains [Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺. The solution turns yellow-green. In a second tube, excess aqueous ammonia is added to [Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺ and a deep blue solution forms. (a) Write an equation for the reaction with concentrated hydrochloric acid. (b) Explain why the coordination number changes. (c) Name the type of reaction that forms [Cu(NH₃)₄(H₂O)₂]²⁺ and describe its structure.
items.answer: (a) [Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺ + 4Cl⁻ ⇌ [CuCl₄]²⁻ + 6H₂O (b) Chloride ions are larger than water molecules, so only four fit around the metal ion. (c) Ligand exchange (substitution); [Cu(NH₃)₄(H₂O)₂]²⁺ is octahedral with four NH₃ in a plane and two H₂O ligands opposite each other.
items.markingKey: (a) [Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺ + 4Cl⁻ ⇌ [CuCl₄]²⁻ + 6H₂O [1] (b) Chloride ions are larger than water molecules, so only four fit around the metal ion [1] (c) ligand exchange [1]; structure [1] [2]

items.stem: Zara adds concentrated hydrochloric acid dropwise to aqueous copper(II) sulfate, which contains [Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺. The solution turns yellow-green. In a second tube, excess aqueous ammonia is added to [Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺ and a deep blue solution forms. (a) State the shape and coordination number of [Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺ and of [CuCl₄]²⁻. (b) Explain why the coordination number changes. (c) Name the type of reaction that forms [Cu(NH₃)₄(H₂O)₂]²⁺ and describe its structure.
items.answer: (a) [Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺: octahedral, 6; [CuCl₄]²⁻: tetrahedral, 4 (b) Chloride ions are larger than water molecules, so only four fit around the metal ion. (c) Ligand exchange (substitution); [Cu(NH₃)₄(H₂O)₂]²⁺ is octahedral with four NH₃ in a plane and two H₂O ligands opposite each other.
items.markingKey: (a) each complex [1] [2] (b) Chloride ions are larger than water molecules, so only four fit around the metal ion [1] (c) ligand exchange [1]; structure [1] [2]

items.stem: Which is the correct definition of the term "polydentate ligand"?
options: A ligand that forms several dative bonds to one metal ion, e.g. hexadentate EDTA⁴⁻.
In complexes, isomerism arising from different spatial arrangements of ligands, such as cis and trans forms.
Isomerism in which two forms are non-superimposable mirror images, e.g. in [Ni(en)₃]²⁺.
A covalent bond in which both electrons of the shared pair come from the same atom (the ligand).
items.answer: A ligand that forms several dative bonds to one metal ion, e.g. hexadentate EDTA⁴⁻.
items.markingKey: Polydentate ligand: a ligand that forms several dative bonds to one metal ion, e.g. hexadentate EDTA⁴⁻.

items.stem: What is the coordination number of the metal ion in [Cu(NH₃)₄(H₂O)₂]²⁺?
items.markingKey: Four NH₃ plus two H₂O.

items.stem: Explain how ligands bond to a central metal ion.
items.answer: Each ligand donates a lone pair of electrons into an empty orbital of the metal ion, forming a dative covalent (coordinate) bond.
items.markingKey: lone pair donated [1]; dative bond to empty orbital [1] [2]

items.stem: Which type of stereoisomerism is shown by [Ni(en)₂(H₂O)₂]²⁺?
items.answer: Geometrical (cis/trans) isomerism
items.markingKey: geometrical (cis/trans) isomerism; the cis isomer also shows optical isomerism.

items.stem: The complex [Ni(en)₃]²⁺ shows stereoisomerism. Identify the type(s) of stereoisomerism and describe the arrangement of the ligands in the isomers.
items.answer: Optical isomerism (non-superimposable mirror images). The ligands span adjacent positions of the octahedron, so the two forms are mirror images that cannot be superimposed.
items.markingKey: type(s) of isomerism [1]; description of arrangement [1]; reference to shape [1] [3]

items.stem: Describe the bonding, shapes and types of isomerism found in transition metal complexes, using named examples.
items.answer: Ligands donate lone pairs (dative bonds); mono-, bi- and polydentate ligands (H₂O, en, EDTA⁴⁻); coordination numbers 2, 4, 6; shapes linear [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺, tetrahedral [CuCl₄]²⁻, square planar cisplatin, octahedral [Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺; cis/trans in [Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂] and [Co(NH₃)₄Cl₂]⁺; optical in [Ni(en)₃]²⁺; cisplatin action.
items.markingKey: dative bonding [1]; ligand types [1]; shapes with examples [2]; geometrical isomerism [1]; optical isomerism [1]; application [1] [7]

items.stem: Ana adds concentrated hydrochloric acid to pink aqueous cobalt(II) chloride, containing [Co(H₂O)₆]²⁺, and the solution turns blue. Adding water reverses the change. (a) Write an equation for the reaction with concentrated hydrochloric acid. (b) State the shape and coordination number of [Co(H₂O)₆]²⁺ and of [CoCl₄]²⁻. (c) Explain why the coordination number changes. (d) Explain why adding water reverses the change.
items.answer: (a) [Co(H₂O)₆]²⁺ + 4Cl⁻ ⇌ [CoCl₄]²⁻ + 6H₂O (b) [Co(H₂O)₆]²⁺: octahedral, 6; [CoCl₄]²⁻: tetrahedral, 4 (c) Chloride ions are larger than water molecules, so only four fit around the metal ion. (d) The equilibrium shifts to the left as [H₂O] increases (and [Cl⁻] decreases), re-forming the hexaaqua ion.
items.markingKey: (a) [Co(H₂O)₆]²⁺ + 4Cl⁻ ⇌ [CoCl₄]²⁻ + 6H₂O [1] (b) each complex [1] [2] (c) Chloride ions are larger than water molecules, so only four fit around the metal ion [1] (d) The equilibrium shifts to the left as [H₂O] increases (and [Cl⁻] decreases) [1]; re-forming the hexaaqua ion [1] [2]

items.stem: Which term is defined as "the observation that different ligands split the d orbitals by different amounts (e.g. NH₃ more than H₂O)"?
items.answer: Spectrochemical effect
items.markingKey: Spectrochemical effect: the observation that different ligands split the d orbitals by different amounts (e.g. NH₃ more than H₂O).

items.stem: Replacing H₂O ligands by NH₃ in a copper(II) complex increases ΔE. What happens to the wavelength of light absorbed?
items.answer: It decreases
items.markingKey: Larger ΔE: higher-energy, shorter-wavelength light.

items.stem: Why are [Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺ and [CuCl₄]²⁻ different colours?
options: One is a solid and one is a solution
Different ligands and geometries give different ΔE, so different wavelengths are absorbed
items.answer: Different ligands and geometries give different ΔE, so different wavelengths are absorbed
items.markingKey: ΔE depends on ligand and shape.

items.stem: The complex [Cr(H₂O)₆]³⁺ absorbs light most strongly at a wavelength of 575 nm. What is the energy gap, ΔE, between the split d orbitals for one ion, in J? (h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹)

The complex [Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺ absorbs light most strongly at a wavelength of 790 nm. Calculate the energy gap, ΔE, between the split d orbitals for one ion, in J. (h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹)

Yusuf uses colorimetry to find the concentration of copper(II) ions in a sample of waste water from a factory in Seoul. Excess aqueous ammonia is added to form the deep blue complex [Cu(NH₃)₄(H₂O)₂]²⁺. Standards give a straight calibration line with absorbance 1.1 at 0.0100 mol dm⁻³ (passing through the origin). The sample gives an absorbance of 0.81. (a) Explain, in terms of d orbitals, why the ammine complex has a different colour from the aqua complex. (b) Explain why a solution of Zn²⁺ ions treated in the same way would give no absorbance in the visible region.
items.answer: (a) NH₃ splits the d orbitals more than H₂O (larger ΔE), so a shorter wavelength of light is absorbed and the transmitted colour changes from pale blue to deep blue. (b) Zn²⁺ is 3d¹⁰; there is no space in the upper d orbitals for an electron to be promoted, so no d–d transitions.
items.markingKey: (a) different ΔE [1]; different wavelength absorbed [1] [2] (b) Zn²⁺ is 3d¹⁰ [1]; there is no space in the upper d orbitals for an electron to be promoted, so no d–d transitions [1] [2]

items.stem: Why is Sc³⁺ colourless in solution?
options: It has no d electrons (3d⁰), so no d–d transitions can occur
Its d orbitals are not split
items.answer: It has no d electrons (3d⁰), so no d–d transitions can occur
items.markingKey: No electrons to promote.

items.stem: Explain why transition metal complexes are often coloured.
items.answer: Ligands split the d orbitals into two energy levels; an electron in a lower d orbital absorbs visible light of energy ΔE and is promoted; the light transmitted/reflected is the complementary colour.
items.markingKey: d orbitals split [1]; absorption of visible light / electron promoted [1]; complementary colour seen [1] [3]

items.stem: A solution of a transition metal complex absorbs light mainly at 505 nm (green). What colour does the solution appear?
items.answer: Red-purple (magenta)
items.markingKey: Absorbs green; transmits the complementary colour, red-purple (magenta).

items.stem: The complex [Co(H₂O)₆]²⁺ absorbs light most strongly at a wavelength of 515 nm. Calculate the energy gap, ΔE, between the split d orbitals for one ion, in J. (h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) Calculate ΔE in kJ mol⁻¹ (L = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹) and predict the colour of the complex.
items.answer: 3.86 × 10⁻¹⁹ J; 233 kJ mol⁻¹; absorbs green light so appears red-purple (magenta) (observed: pink)
items.markingKey: ΔE = hc/λ [1]; λ = 515 × 10⁻⁹ m [1]; ΔE = 3.86 × 10⁻¹⁹ J [1]; × L ÷ 1000 = 233 kJ mol⁻¹ [1]; absorbs green, appears red-purple (magenta) [1] [5]

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "the logarithm of the stability constant, used to compare stabilities of complexes because Kstab values are very large"?
items.answer: Log Kstab
items.markingKey: Log Kstab: the logarithm of the stability constant, used to compare stabilities of complexes because Kstab values are very large.

items.stem: Why does EDTA⁴⁻ readily replace six water ligands around Cu²⁺?
options: The number of particles increases from 2 to 7, so entropy increases (chelate effect)
Cu–O bonds are weaker than Cu–N bonds
items.answer: The number of particles increases from 2 to 7, so entropy increases (chelate effect)
items.markingKey: ΔS positive, ΔG negative.

items.stem: Carbon monoxide is toxic because
options: it forms a more stable complex with the Fe²⁺ in haemoglobin than O₂ does
items.answer: it forms a more stable complex with the Fe²⁺ in haemoglobin than O₂ does
items.markingKey: Higher Kstab for CO; ligand exchange.

items.stem: For the equilibrium [Ni(H₂O)₆]²⁺ + 6NH₃ ⇌ [Ni(NH₃)₆]²⁺ + 6H₂O, the equilibrium concentrations are [[Ni(NH₃)₆]²⁺] = 0.02, [[Ni(H₂O)₆]²⁺] = 5.02 × 10⁻⁵ and [NH₃] = 0.1 mol dm⁻³. What is the value of Kstab?

For the equilibrium [Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺ + 4NH₃ ⇌ [Cu(NH₃)₄(H₂O)₂]²⁺ + 4H₂O, the equilibrium concentrations are [[Cu(NH₃)₄(H₂O)₂]²⁺] = 0.1, [[Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺] = 7.94 × 10⁻¹⁵ and [NH₃] = 1 mol dm⁻³. Calculate Kstab and give its units.
items.answer: 1.26 × 10¹³ dm¹² mol⁻⁴
items.markingKey: Kstab = [[Cu(NH₃)₄(H₂O)₂]²⁺] ÷ ([[Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺][NH₃]⁴) [1]; = 0.1 ÷ (7.94 × 10⁻¹⁵ × 1⁴) = 1.26 × 10¹³ [1]; units dm¹² mol⁻⁴ [1] [3]

items.stem: Chloe investigates ligand exchange in copper(II) complexes. log Kstab: [Cu(NH₃)₄(H₂O)₂]²⁺ 13.1; [CuCl₄]²⁻ 5.6; [Cu(EDTA)]²⁻ 18.8. (a) Write an equation for the reaction of [Cu(NH₃)₄(H₂O)₂]²⁺ with EDTA⁴⁻ and explain why it occurs. (b) Suggest why EDTA is used in the treatment of heavy-metal poisoning.
items.answer: (a) [Cu(NH₃)₄(H₂O)₂]²⁺ + EDTA⁴⁻ → [Cu(EDTA)]²⁻ + 4NH₃ + 2H₂O; [Cu(EDTA)]²⁻ is more stable (larger Kstab); particles increase from 2 to 7 so ΔS is positive (chelate effect). (b) It forms very stable, soluble chelates with metal ions (large Kstab), which can be excreted.
items.markingKey: (a) equation [1]; Kstab [1]; entropy / chelate effect [1] [3] (b) It forms very stable, soluble chelates with metal ions (large Kstab), which can be excreted [1]

items.stem: Explain how log Kstab values are used to predict whether a ligand exchange reaction occurs.
items.answer: A ligand will replace another if the new complex has a larger Kstab (more stable); the equilibrium lies towards the complex with the larger stability constant.
items.markingKey: A ligand will replace another if the new complex has a larger Kstab (more stable) [1]; the equilibrium lies towards the complex with the larger stability constant [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain the chelate effect using the reaction of [Ni(H₂O)₆]²⁺ with ethane-1,2-diamine.
items.answer: [Ni(H₂O)₆]²⁺ + 3en → [Ni(en)₃]²⁺ + 6H₂O; 4 particles become 7, so ΔS is positive; ΔH is small (similar Ni–N bonds), so ΔG is negative and the chelate is much more stable.
items.markingKey: equation / particle count [1]; ΔS positive [1]; ΔG negative [1] [3]

items.stem: log Kstab: [Ni(NH₃)₆]²⁺ 8.6; [Ni(en)₃]²⁺ 18.3. Predict what happens when en is added to a solution containing [Ni(NH₃)₆]²⁺. Explain your answer and write an equation.
items.answer: Ligand exchange: [Ni(en)₃]²⁺ forms because it has the larger Kstab (more stable complex); [Ni(NH₃)₆]²⁺ + 3en → [Ni(en)₃]²⁺ + 6NH₃ (with water as needed).
items.markingKey: [Ni(en)₃]²⁺ forms [1]; larger Kstab / more stable [1]; equation [1] [3]

items.stem: Felix investigates ligand exchange in copper(II) complexes. log Kstab: [Cu(NH₃)₄(H₂O)₂]²⁺ 13.1; [CuCl₄]²⁻ 5.6; [Cu(EDTA)]²⁻ 18.8. (a) Predict what is observed when excess aqueous ammonia is added to a yellow-green solution of [CuCl₄]²⁻. Explain using the data. (b) Write an equation for the reaction of [Cu(NH₃)₄(H₂O)₂]²⁺ with EDTA⁴⁻ and explain why it occurs. (c) Suggest why EDTA is used in the treatment of heavy-metal poisoning.
items.answer: (a) The solution turns deep blue as [Cu(NH₃)₄(H₂O)₂]²⁺ forms, because it has a much larger Kstab than [CuCl₄]²⁻. (b) [Cu(NH₃)₄(H₂O)₂]²⁺ + EDTA⁴⁻ → [Cu(EDTA)]²⁻ + 4NH₃ + 2H₂O; [Cu(EDTA)]²⁻ is more stable (larger Kstab); particles increase from 2 to 7 so ΔS is positive (chelate effect). (c) It forms very stable, soluble chelates with metal ions (large Kstab), which can be excreted.
items.markingKey: (a) deep blue [1]; Kstab comparison [1] [2] (b) equation [1]; Kstab [1]; entropy / chelate effect [1] [3] (c) It forms very stable, soluble chelates with metal ions (large Kstab), which can be excreted [1]

items.stem: Which term is defined as "an oxidising agent, Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 14H⁺ + 6e⁻ → 2Cr³⁺ + 7H₂O, orange changing to green"?
items.answer: Acidified potassium dichromate(VI)
items.markingKey: Acidified potassium dichromate(VI): an oxidising agent, Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 14H⁺ + 6e⁻ → 2Cr³⁺ + 7H₂O, orange changing to green.

items.stem: What is the mole ratio MnO₄⁻ : C₂O₄²⁻ in the titration of ethanedioate ions?
items.markingKey: 2MnO₄⁻ + 5C₂O₄²⁻ + 16H⁺ → 2Mn²⁺ + 10CO₂ + 8H₂O.

items.stem: In the titration of ethanedioate with MnO₄⁻, the reaction speeds up after the first few drops because
options: Mn²⁺ formed acts as a catalyst (autocatalysis)
items.answer: Mn²⁺ formed acts as a catalyst (autocatalysis)
items.markingKey: Product catalyses the reaction.

items.stem: 17.70 cm³ of 0.01 mol dm⁻³ potassium manganate(VII) reacted with 25.0 cm³ of a solution containing Fe²⁺ ions. Equation: MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5Fe²⁺ → Mn²⁺ + 5Fe³⁺ + 4H₂O. How many moles of Fe²⁺ were in the 25.0 cm³ sample?

34.05 cm³ of 0.015 mol dm⁻³ potassium manganate(VII) reacted with 25.0 cm³ of a solution of ethanedioate ions. Equation: 2MnO₄⁻ + 5C₂O₄²⁻ + 16H⁺ → 2Mn²⁺ + 10CO₂ + 8H₂O. Calculate the concentration of C₂O₄²⁻ in the sample.
items.answer: 0.0511 mol dm⁻³

items.stem: 32.75 cm³ of 0.02 mol dm⁻³ potassium dichromate(VI) reacted with 25.0 cm³ of a solution containing Fe²⁺ ions. Equation: Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 14H⁺ + 6Fe²⁺ → 2Cr³⁺ + 6Fe³⁺ + 7H₂O. Calculate the concentration of Fe²⁺ in the sample. The 25.0 cm³ sample was taken from 250 cm³ of solution made by dissolving iron tablets in dilute sulfuric acid. Calculate the total mass of iron in the tablets.
items.answer: 0.157 mol dm⁻³; mass of iron = 2.19 g

items.stem: Describe how redox titrations with acidified potassium manganate(VII) and potassium dichromate(VI) are used to determine the amount of iron(II) in a sample, including equations, end points and a specimen calculation.
items.answer: Half-equations MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5e⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O, Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 14H⁺ + 6e⁻ → 2Cr³⁺ + 7H₂O, Fe²⁺ → Fe³⁺ + e⁻; overall equations and ratios 1:5 and 1:6; sulfuric acid not HCl; MnO₄⁻ self-indicating (pale pink), dichromate needs redox indicator; procedure; calculation from titre to moles to mass/percentage; sources of error (air oxidation).
items.markingKey: half-equations and ratios [2]; acid choice [1]; end points [1]; procedure [1]; calculation [2] [7]

items.stem: Ana in a research laboratory analyses an iron supplement. 2.59 g of crushed tablets were dissolved in dilute sulfuric acid and made up to 250 cm³. 25.0 cm³ portions were titrated with 0.015 mol dm⁻³ potassium manganate(VII); the mean titre was 21.50 cm³. (a) Explain why dilute sulfuric acid is used rather than hydrochloric acid. (b) State how the end point is detected. (c) Suggest why the results might underestimate the iron content if the solution was left in air for a long time before titration.
items.answer: (a) The oxidising agent would oxidise Cl⁻ ions to chlorine, using extra titrant and giving a high titre. (b) Colourless to pale pink. (c) Some Fe²⁺ is oxidised by air to Fe³⁺, which does not react with the titrant, so the titre is lower.
items.markingKey: (a) The oxidising agent would oxidise Cl⁻ ions to chlorine [1]; using extra titrant and giving a high titre [1] [2] (b) Colourless to pale pink [1] (c) any 2 from: Some Fe²⁺ is oxidised by air to Fe³⁺; which does not react with the titrant; so the titre is lower (1 mark each) [2]

items.stem: What is the mole ratio MnO₄⁻ : Fe²⁺ in an acidified redox titration?
items.markingKey: MnO₄⁻ gains 5e⁻; each Fe²⁺ loses 1e⁻.

items.stem: Which is the correct definition of the term "iodometric titration"?
options: A strong oxidising agent, MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5e⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O, used in redox titrations.

items.stem: Explain why zinc is a d-block element but not a transition element.
items.answer: Its outermost electrons are in the 3d/4s region (d block), but its only ion Zn²⁺ has a complete 3d¹⁰ subshell, so it does not form an ion with an incomplete d subshell.

items.answer: (a) 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d¹⁰ 4s¹ (b) +2; 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d⁹ (c) It provides an alternative route with lower activation energy, by adsorbing reactants on its surface (using d orbitals) and/or changing oxidation state in intermediate steps. (d) Yes: copper in the +2 state has 1 unpaired electron(s).

items.stem: Mateo adds concentrated hydrochloric acid dropwise to aqueous copper(II) sulfate, which contains [Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺. The solution turns yellow-green. In a second tube, excess aqueous ammonia is added to [Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺ and a deep blue solution forms. (a) Explain why adding water reverses the change. (b) Name the type of reaction that forms [Cu(NH₃)₄(H₂O)₂]²⁺ and describe its structure.
items.answer: (a) The equilibrium shifts to the left as [H₂O] increases (and [Cl⁻] decreases), re-forming the hexaaqua ion. (b) Ligand exchange (substitution); [Cu(NH₃)₄(H₂O)₂]²⁺ is octahedral with four NH₃ in a plane and two H₂O ligands opposite each other.

items.stem: State what is meant by the term d-orbital splitting.
items.answer: The separation of the five d orbitals of a metal ion into groups of different energy when ligands approach.

items.stem: Explain why the splitting in a tetrahedral complex is smaller than in an octahedral complex.
items.answer: In a tetrahedral complex fewer ligands are present and none point directly at the d orbitals, so the repulsion difference between orbitals is smaller.

Explain why the Kstab of the haemoglobin–CO complex is important in carbon monoxide poisoning.
items.answer: CO binds to Fe²⁺ in haemoglobin far more strongly than O₂ (larger Kstab); ligand exchange of O₂ by CO is effectively irreversible, so oxygen transport is reduced.

items.stem: For the equilibrium [Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺ + 4NH₃ ⇌ [Cu(NH₃)₄(H₂O)₂]²⁺ + 4H₂O, the equilibrium concentrations are [[Cu(NH₃)₄(H₂O)₂]²⁺] = 0.1, [[Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺] = 1.27 × 10⁻¹³ and [NH₃] = 0.5 mol dm⁻³. Calculate Kstab and give its units.
items.answer: 1.26 × 10¹³ dm¹² mol⁻⁴
